copies.headline: John's Rams Stack Is The Undefeated's Problem
copies.body:
Adam is 6-0 with an 89% all-play and the league's best scoring average, which is the kind of profile that doesn't usually need a caveat. Here's one anyway: John owns the better roster this week. The Rams stack of Stafford, Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua is playing in the week's second-highest total at Las Vegas, and Nacua alone at 25 is the biggest single projection on either side. Tight end is the quiet separator — Brock Bowers at 18 with Trey McBride at 16 behind him means John can absorb the questionable tag without blinking. Adam's LaPorta at 13 doesn't answer that.
Adam's counter is receiver depth: Smith-Njigba, Olave and Coker clear John's third and fourth wideouts, where DeMario Douglas and Malik Washington at 10 apiece are thin. But Smith-Njigba is in a 42.5 game, Olave's Saints are home dogs, and the Bucky Irving and Rico Dowdle tags leave Kenneth Walker carrying the backfield in the week's lowest-scoring environment. The undefeated run ends on volume John can't be talked out of.

copies.headline: Isaac's Top Six Hide A Hollow Roster
copies.body:
The positional math is nearly even — Logan edges QB, WR and tight end on best-available, Isaac takes running back by two — which means this comes down to who survives the back half of the lineup. Isaac's does not survive. Terry McLaurin is out, Jakobi Meyers and Dalton Kincaid project zero, and the third receiver is Kalif Raymond at five. If Saquon Barkley's questionable tag turns bad against Philadelphia's front, Isaac is starting J.K. Dobbins and hoping. Logan's worst decision is choosing between Aaron Rodgers and Joe Burrow, and his sixth-best receiver is Rashid Shaheed.
The game script helps Logan too. Malik Nabers is Isaac's second-best asset and the Giants are 10.5-point dogs in a 42.5 game — garbage-time volume, not touchdowns. Meanwhile Logan has Pittsburgh laid over Jaylen Warren, Rodgers and Germie Bernard in a 44.5-point spot. Isaac scores 99.8 a week and is last in all-play at 26 percent for a reason: there's no floor beneath the stars.

copies.headline: Christian Keeps Scoring, Keeps Losing, Meets Grant
copies.body:
The receiver room is the whole game. Grant's top three — Amon-Ra St. Brown, Christian Watson and Zay Flowers — project 52 to Christian's 46, and two of those sit in the week's best environment: Detroit-Green Bay at 53.5, the only total on the board that looks like actual football. Christian's answer is CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith in a 44.5 Dallas-Philly game where Dallas is favored, plus Jameson Williams fighting St. Brown for the same targets. Christian does win tight end by six with George Kittle in San Francisco's 49.5-point trip to Atlanta, and Jordan Love edges Kyler Murray, whose Vikings are in a 41.5 mudfight with Indianapolis.
Backfields wash at 27 apiece, but the risk isn't even: Quinshon Judkins is questionable and Grant's next man is Bam Knight at 7. Christian has Chase Brown, Aaron Jones and a questionable Kamara. The real difference is that Christian is the better team — 127.7 a game, 4th in all-play, minus-1.5 in luck — and Grant, 9th in scoring with a 26-40 all-play, has been getting away with it.

copies.headline: Leif's Bye Week Quarterback Problem Decides This
copies.body:
Leif has Josh Allen and nobody else, and Allen projects for zero. That is a 15-point hole before anyone touches the ball, and it's not a lineup choice — it's the whole quarterback room. The backfield pays some of it back: McCaffrey (22) in a 49.5-total game at Atlanta and Derrick Henry (20) against Cincinnati in a 48.5 shootout give Leif a 42-30 edge on the two best backs, and if SF-ATL goes the way Vegas thinks, McCaffrey is the ceiling. But the receivers are a disaster. Chris Godwin at 9 is the best of it, with Adams on IR, Diggs at zero, and Evans and Douglas both tagged.
CJ's top three wideouts clear Leif's by 15. Metcalf gets a Steelers team favored in a 44.5 game, and Egbuka, if the tag clears, is in a three-point Tampa game that should stay open. The injury tags on Mayfield and Egbuka are the real risk here, and Jonathan Taylor as a 6.5-point dog in a 41.5 total is the kind of game script that produces 11 points instead of 18. Still, CJ wins three of four positional groups and doesn't have to start a quarterback who isn't playing.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 4-2 Finally Meets Its Reckoning
copies.body:
Mitchell is 1-5 and still the better team here, which is the whole story. Kaleb's 105.5 a game ranks 10th, his all-play is 24-42, and he's carrying +1.8 wins of luck he hasn't earned — the last three weeks are 109.6, 85.7, 94.4. The gap is at running back and it's bigger than the five projected points suggest: Jahmyr Gibbs in a 53.5-total divisional game against Green Bay is the best asset on either side, while Kaleb needs a questionable Breece Hall in a 39.5-total Jets-Dolphins slog and Ashton Jeanty as a 3.5-point dog.
Receiver is closer than it looks because of tags. Matthew Golden and DJ Moore are both questionable, so Mitchell could be down to Nico Collins against the Giants and Courtland Sutton. Kaleb's answer is Drake London in a 49.5-total game he'll likely be chasing in, then Carnell Tate and Jordan Addison, neither of whom has a usable floor. Travis Kelce questionable hurts, but Harold Fannin Jr. isn't a real counterpunch.

copies.headline: Noah's Backfield Isn't Showing Up To Work
copies.body:
The running back gap decides this one. Peter's best two, Bijan Robinson (19) and Josh Jacobs (13), are worth 32; Noah counters with Rhamondre Stevenson (12) and Kendre Miller (9) while James Cook III sits on a bye and Mike Washington Jr. is questionable. That's an 11-point hole with no depth to patch it, and Bijan has the best game environment on either roster — Atlanta a 2.5-point dog in a 49.5 total, which means volume and late targets. Noah's receivers are a committee of 11-to-15-point guys with Jordyn Tyson on IR; Peter's A.J. Brown and Tee Higgins carry real ceilings, Higgins in a 48.5-point Bengals-Ravens game.
The caveat is Lamar Jackson's questionable tag, and it's a real one. If Lamar sits, J.J. McCarthy (16) is a competent replacement but his Giants are 10.5-point dogs in Houston, which is garbage-time points at best. Peter has been outrunning his process all year (+1.5 luck wins, 69.8 last week), but Noah at 1-5 with a 30% all-play isn't the team to punish it.

intro: Adam is the only unbeaten left and he draws the toughest assignment on the board, with John favored on the road in a game that could finally put a loss on the 6-0 line and bunch up the top of the standings. The closest call is CJ at Leif, two 4-2 teams with nearly identical résumés separated by a few snaps of running back usage, and the winner slides into second while the loser falls back into the wild-card scrum. Mitchell, meanwhile, gets Kaleb and is actually favored, which is the kind of sentence 1-5 teams wait all year to read.
